efficiencyGuidance.purpose: Avoid needless authoring-turn repetition without skipping required validation or approval.
rules: Reuse unchanged IDs, bindings, responses, source, schemas and results; do not reread or restate them without a reason.
Before retrying a failed command or tool, inspect the error and contract; retry only after a concrete correction or allowed idempotent reconciliation.
Batch related read-only checks and return concise diffs or summaries instead of repeating unchanged logs or intermediate reports.
Never skip required tests, validation, human approval or safety checks for efficiency.

must: Treat accepted=true as the aggregate verdict for client, environment, canonicalMcpUrl, onboardingProfileId, release, contract and required capabilities; do not independently revalidate the same fields without a contradictory observation.

For accepted=false, classify problems and correct a request or parser in the same tool flow before halting; halt only for a true unresolved compatibility, connection or explicit invocation-limit blocker.

Parse MCP CallToolResult by checking isError first and then reading structuredContent; only when structuredContent is absent, parse one JSON text content item once; use structuredContent.environmentBinding and structuredContent.proposal.id as the canonical paths.
Use the environmentBinding returned by the successful handshake for every later SDK tool call.
Verify sdkIdentity on every post-handshake SDK response; do not require post-handshake sdkIdentity on the handshake response itself.

Treat accountContext.accountRef, environment and contextVersion from the handshake or a read response as the canonical MCP account context; do not infer the actual account from user wording, a creator slug, a display name or a Portal URL.

Before every owner-bound write, show the actual MCP account and target creator once and pass the same accountRef as expectedAccountRef; missing, stale, different-account or different-environment values must fail closed before persistence.
Create a game draft and wait for human module profile confirmation before implementing prototype UI or AppSet source.
Bind shared source to moduleProfileRevision, moduleContractDigest, SDK version and delivery-specific usage evidence.
Build the interactive prototype and formal package from the same game source with different adapters.
Show the published prototype URL, module usage matrix and review checklist, then wait for explicit human approval.
Use server-side Node-free validation and packaging when the authoring host has no Node.js.
After preparing a module profile proposal, read it back in the same tool flow with the same requestId before waiting for Portal owner approval.

If a proposal outcome is unknown, reparse the retained result and then use at most one same-requestId identical-payload replay when the explicit invocation limit permits; never create a second logical proposal for reconciliation.
mustNot: Treat MCP Connected, tool discovery, a URL, or the shared Shell alone as workflow completion.
Switch production and development inside one authoring chat or session.
Reuse creator IDs, game IDs, revisions, URLs or environment bindings across semantic environments.
Implement or publish a prototype before human module profile confirmation.
Publish a formal package before the current module-bound prototype revision has human approval.
Replace a required SDK module with bespoke game code or require fictitious imports for platform-owned modules.
Ask a general creator to install Node.js, npm, Git or Vercel CLI as the default completion path.
Request or persist passwords, tokens, Cookies, MFA codes or Vercel credentials.

mockQuality.purpose: Human operation and review of the module-bound interactive prototype built from the same shared source as the formal package.
rejected: missing selectable target or observable action result
static HTML without shared SDK source
required module replaced by bespoke UI or logic
